title: Friday the 13th Part 2
tagline: Camp's open again. Lock the cabin door behind you.
about: Five years after the Camp Crystal Lake murders, a new group of counsellors trains beside the lake, not knowing someone is watching from the woods.
cue: Serve the bar nuts and onion rings when Paul gathers the counsellors around the campfire to tell the legend.

    StartersLast night in town spiced bar nutsMixed nuts roasted with brown sugar, smoked paprika, cayenne and rosemaryHow to make it400g mixed raw nuts30g butter, melted2 tbsp brown sugar1 tsp smoked paprika1/4 tsp cayenne pepper1 tbsp rosemary leaves, finely chopped1 tsp sea salt flakesHeat the oven to 170°C and line a tray with baking paper.Toss 400g mixed nuts with 30g melted butter, 2 tbsp brown sugar, the paprika, cayenne and rosemary.Spread on the tray and roast, stirring halfway, until golden and fragrant.Sprinkle with the salt and leave to cool on the tray so the coating sets crisp.Crystal Lake beer-battered onion ringsThick onion rings in a crisp beer batter with smoky chipotle mayoHow to make it2 large brown onions, sliced into thick rings150g plain flour50g cornflour1 tsp baking powder1 tsp salt250ml cold lager1 L vegetable oil, for frying120g mayonnaise1 tsp chipotle chilli powderSeparate the onion rings and toss in 2 tbsp of the flour.Whisk the rest of the flour with the cornflour, baking powder and salt, then whisk in 250ml cold lager to a thick batter.Heat the oil in a deep pot to 180°C.Dip the rings in the batter and fry in batches for about 3 minutes until golden, then drain on paper towel.Stir the chipotle powder into the mayonnaise and serve with the hot rings.Pickled eggs with hot sauceTed stays for another. Best call he makes.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsCamp Blood chilli con carneSlow-cooked beef chilli with kidney beans, chipotle and cumin, with rice, sour cream and cheddarHow to make it1 tbsp vegetable oil800g beef chuck, cut into 2cm pieces1 large onion, diced3 garlic cloves, crushed1 red capsicum, diced2 tsp ground cumin2 tsp smoked paprika2 tsp chipotle chilli powder1 tsp dried oregano2 tbsp tomato paste800g canned crushed tomatoes375ml beef stock1 tsp salt400g can kidney beans, drained1 1/2 cups long-grain rice150g sour cream100g cheddar, gratedHeat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot and brown 800g diced beef chuck in batches over high heat, then lift out.Turn the heat down and fry the onion, garlic and red capsicum in the same pot until soft.Stir in 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 2 tsp chipotle powder, 1 tsp oregano and 2 tbsp tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.Return the beef with 800g crushed tomatoes, 375ml beef stock and 1 tsp salt, cover and simmer on low until the beef falls apart.Add the drained kidney beans and simmer uncovered until thick. Meanwhile rinse 1.5 cups rice and simmer with 2.25 cups water, covered, until the water is absorbed.Serve the chilli over the rice with a spoon of sour cream and a handful of grated cheddar.SweetsSack-head s'mores barsCrushed biscuit base, milk chocolate ganache and a toasted marshmallow top, cut into barsHow to make it250g plain sweet biscuits, crushed100g butter, melted200g milk chocolate, chopped100ml thickened cream250g white marshmallowsMix the crushed biscuits with the melted butter and press firmly into a lined 20cm square tin.Chill until firm.Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate, stir until smooth and spread over the base.Chill until set.Cover with the marshmallows and grill on high until toasted, watching closely.Cool for a few minutes and cut into 12 bars with a hot knife.DrinksCrystal Lake bourbon lemonadeBourbon, fresh lemon and honey syrup over ice, topped with sodaHow to make it180ml bourbon4 lemons, juiced80ml honey80ml boiling water400ml soda water, chilled1 bag ice1 lemon, slicedStir the honey into the boiling water until dissolved and leave to cool.Shake the bourbon, lemon juice and honey syrup hard with a handful of ice.Strain into 4 ice-filled glasses, top with soda water and add a lemon slice.Pitcher of draught beerPaul calls Jason an urban legend.
